Definition: from G1053; Galatic or relating to Galatia:--of Galatia.
BiblicalUsage: Galatic means of Galatia, belonging to that region. Paul and his company went throughout Phrygia and the region of Galatia in Acts 16:6, forbidden by the Holy Ghost to preach in Asia, and later he went over all the country of Galatia and Phrygia in order, strengthening all the disciples, in Acts 18:23. The word marks the ground Paul walked to strengthen the churches.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the strengthening of disciples is the quiet work of the apostle; Paul went over the country in order, church by church, and I hold that the gospel spreads not only by preaching but by returning to strengthen those already won.
